Our flagship initiative

Christmas in the Street

Every December, we close the year the way we think it should end: a party for children, health checks for the adults who bring them, and foodstuffs for the widows and market women in the community.

3 editions runEdition 4 · This December
Volunteer For Edition 4

One Saturday. Three ways we show up.

What happens on the day.

  • Kids' Christmas Party

    A full party thrown for children in the community: games, food, gifts and the kind of afternoon that becomes a memory.

  • Health On The Spot

    Free blood pressure checks for the adults who come with them, a small practical way to look after the grown-ups too.

  • Foodstuffs For Women

    Raw foodstuffs handed directly to widows, mothers and market women in the community, starting with rice, growing every year since.

Edition 4

This December

Children reached, edition over edition.

In pictures

Moments worth keeping.

Photos are shared with the consent of parents and guardians.

Edition 1, in their own words:

We planned for 50 children. We got blessed with 150 and still had to turn some away disappointed.

That feeling, grateful for how many came and aching for the ones we couldn’t fit, is a big part of why Project 1,000 Smiles exists: so reach doesn’t have to wait for one Saturday in December.

Edition 3

Beyond the party.

The joy of being remembered

Every child left with a gift in hand and a reason to smile. Santa made sure no one went home empty-handed, and no child felt forgotten.

Smiles all around

Santa had a gift and a kind word for every child who came to see him. There were hugs, laughter and big bright smiles, because on this day, every child was welcome and every child was celebrated.
